reason: Picks the correct definition of component VaR as a partition summing to portfolio VaR, against distractors on marginal and individual VaR.
Diversification benefit as undiversified minus diversified VaR for a three-asset portfolio.
Reading undiversified VaR for a long/short book: it is the upper bound at correlation minus one, not plus one.
Individual VaR (absolute position) and signed component VaR of a short leg, via individual VaR times rho.
Marginal VaR of one asset from the covariance matrix, alpha times (Sigma x)_i over portfolio dollar volatility.
Which statements about marginal VaR hold: unitless, alpha cov over sigma_p equals (VaR/W) beta, sign follows covariance.
Incremental VaR of a multi-factor trade by the marginal VaR shortcut, sum of marginal VaR times exposure change.
Marginal VaR shortcut versus full revaluation for incremental VaR: shortcut suits small trades, a large trade needs revaluation.
Component VaR (tangent) versus exact VaR reduction from deleting a position (curve), with component VaR computed from the formula.
Percent contribution of a negatively correlated asset via component VaR equals individual VaR times rho over portfolio VaR.
Properties of component VaR: sums to portfolio VaR, equals individual VaR times rho, and differs from individual-VaR shares.
Simulation-based component VaR from averaged scenario P&L; the notes explicitly leave simulation-based component VaR unselected.
Tangent (marginal, component) versus curve (incremental deletion) on the VaR chart, the tangent-versus-curve shape.
Why risk systems report marginal VaR alongside individual VaR; general rationale with no specific calculation or allocation rule tested.
Cut the position with the highest marginal VaR; with a common VaR/W factor only beta ranks, then VaR change.
Fully invested switch: cut the highest marginal VaR, add to the lowest, and compute the first-order VaR change.
Minimum risk is reached when all marginal VaRs (betas) are equal, so no small reallocation lowers VaR.
Negative marginal VaR on a short leg is misread as a hedge; component VaR (marginal times position) shows it adds risk.
Incremental VaR of a client trade by the marginal VaR shortcut, marginal VaR times trade size, to adjust the quote.
Shortcut incremental VaR of a multi-leg rebalancing as the sum of marginal VaR times exposure change.
Marginal VaR times position as a precise estimate of liquidating a 45% holding: shortcut misused on a large trade.
Choose the cut by highest marginal VaR, not largest component VaR or contribution, then compute the new VaR.
Compute marginal VaRs of two assets and shift from the higher to the lower to reduce VaR.
Choose the asset to add with the lowest marginal VaR (alpha rho sigma) and compute the first-order VaR increase.
Risk-minimizing weight where marginal VaRs are equal, and the common marginal VaR at that position.
